g-115-10641.title: Fix: the zakpod1 monitor's controls never reach cc-07 on their own - nothing on cc-07 pulls world/, so conf edits (incl. a MUTE_UNTIL set today) and script fixes silently do not take effect
g-115-10641.description:
MEASURED 2026-09-22 ~23:10-23:20 UTC by alpha (cc-04) while executing g-115-10635 (owner directive: zakpod1 fan false alarms).

1. The authoritative store copy of world/scripts/zakpod1-health.conf carried MUTE_UNTIL=2026-09-23T01:00 (version 3e487f0e..., 2443 B; writer not recorded - no changelog row, no board post). cc-07, where the monitor runs, still had the 14:20 conf (2440 B, md5 07f3b29a..., MUTE_UNTIL blank). So whoever set that mute believed it was in force, and it never was.
2. The same held for the script: cc-07 kept the 21:36 copy of zakpod1-health-check.py after the store moved; alpha delivered both files by hand (scp + atomic mv, md5 == store) with backups at /var/lib/zakpod1-health/*.bak-20260922-pre-fan-rule.

4. Both the conf header ("the copy on cc-07 updates within a few minutes") and the script docstring CONTROLS section promise propagation. As measured that promise is false: an owner edit to EMAIL / MUTE_UNTIL / any threshold does not take effect until someone copies the file.

UNMEASURED remedy options (retrieve against the remedy before choosing - rb-5669): (a) load_conf reads through the storage backend each check (covers the CONF, not code); (b) a small pull step/timer on cc-07 for world/scripts/zakpod1-* before each check; (c) at minimum, correct the two false propagation claims. g-115-5136.title: Idea: team-state session_ended is write-only-false — no writer sets it true anywhere
g-115-5136.description:
MEASURED 2026-08-06 (zeta, hostname cc-02, uname -r 6.8.0-136-generic) during g-115-5079. Unsuppressed grep for the token session_ended across the framework -- no head, no tail, no 2>/dev/null -- returns exactly ONE writer, and it writes the literal false. Nothing sets it true. My own live row confirms it: the value is False on an agent that has ended many sessions.

THE FALSE CLAIM TO FIX OR RETIRE: the same skill that carries that write also states in a comment that /stop sets the value true, and justifies its own write as clearing a stale true. There is no such writer. So the write clears a value that is already false and can never be otherwise, and the comment tells the next reader a mechanism exists that does not.

WHY MEDIUM: no measured consumer reads it to decide anything -- the only other mention is a docstring listing row keys. Present harm is a misleading comment plus a dead field, not a wrong decision. But the name advertises a liveness signal a partner might reasonably start reading, and it would be permanently wrong if they did.

DECIDE, DO NOT JUST PATCH. Two honest options: (a) give it a true-writer on the stop path, or (b) retire the field, its false-write, and the comment. Pick (a) only if a consumer is actually wanted; (b) is the subtraction. Doing (a) without correcting the comment leaves it wrong in a new way.

NOT MEASURED: whether any domain script or peer deployment reads it. Check before choosing (b).

VERIFICATION: either a true-writer exists on the stop path and the comment describes it accurately, or field plus write plus comment are all gone. Re-run the same unsuppressed grep; it must return a self-consistent picture.

g-115-9688.title: Serialize holder_since on GET /v1/admin/runner-claims so a claim handover is observable to CLI consumers
g-115-9688.description: DISCOVERED during g-115-9599 (runner-claim status reported NOT-RUNNING for a working Body). WHAT: owncloud_backend.py computes and stores holder_since on every RunnerClaim — it is stamped ONLY by acquire_runner attempt 2, i.e. precisely on a TENURE CHANGE (attempt 1, the same-machine re-acquire, deliberately does not touch it, per g-306-379). That is exactly the signal needed to answer "did this claim just change hands?". mind_api/src/endpoints/admin.py:645 serializes only {agent, machine_id, agent_state, heartbeat_at, runner_token_fp} — holder_since is dropped at the endpoint boundary, so NO CLI consumer can see it. WHY IT MATTERS: g-115-9599 established that machine_id on a non-RUNNING row is a TOMBSTONE (the last holder, not a location), so two consecutive NOT-RUNNING readings naming different boxes are two stand-downs and are indistinguishable from a handover using the fields currently exposed. That ambiguity is what produced a false fleet-down report to the owner on 2026-09-10. g-115-9599 fixed the SENTENCE (the line now labels the tombstone and states its scope, rc unchanged at 4) and explicitly DECLINED to add a migrating/UNKNOWN verdict, because it would need this field. This goal is that precondition, and nothing more. TREE CONSULTATION: tree-find-node.sh --text "runner claim lease holder liveness endpoint serialization" --leaf-only --top 3 returned no relevant node (top hit zakcode-permission-model, score 5.09) — this surface has no tree node; the nearest knowledge is core/config/conventions/partner-liveness.md, whose section 3b g-115-9599 added and which names this gap in its closing paragraph. SCOPE NOTE: serializing the field is a one-line endpoint change plus a consumer. Do NOT also change runner-claim status rc values — worker_reducer_liveness.py and reducer_self_fence.py consume rc=4 in OPPOSITE fail-safe directions (decisive vs inert), and that divergence is pinned by test_reducer_self_fence.py against the real worker module.

g-115-9367.title: Teach provision-processor-venv.sh a Scripts/ vs bin/ branch so --check reports NOT-APPLICABLE rather than NOT-PROVISIONED on non-POSIX
g-115-9367.description:
CASE A SUCCESSOR — filed by alpha worker Body d662c0a6 on DESKTOP-O91DLK2 (MINGW64_NT-10.0-19045), 2026-09-07, carrying the explicitly-separable remainder of g-115-9360 rather than dropping it. g-115-9360's own text names this: 'SECOND, SEPARABLE QUESTION for whoever takes this: whether the provisioner should ALSO learn a Scripts/ vs bin/ branch so --check reports NOT-APPLICABLE rather than NOT-PROVISIONED on non-POSIX. That is the deeper fix and is NOT required to stop the mis-offer.'

THE MIS-OFFER IS ALREADY STOPPED, so this is quality, not urgency: g-115-9360 added the box-must-be-linux command_succeeds precondition to g-115-6209 and verified it live (pre-fix rank 954 of 1830 on this box; post-fix absent, blocked view reading 'block_reason: precondition_unmet / Preconditions unmet: box-must-be-linux'). Do NOT re-do that work.

WHAT REMAINS. world/scripts/provision-processor-venv.sh hardcodes the POSIX venv layout — VENV/bin/python at lines 47/117/123/130 — while `py -3 -m venv` on Windows produces Scripts/python.exe and no bin/ at all (measured directly on this box). So --check cannot succeed there and cannot distinguish 'this box needs the venv' from 'this box can never have one in that layout'. It reports NOT-PROVISIONED where the truthful answer is NOT-APPLICABLE.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS WITH THE GATE IN PLACE: the selector-level fix suppresses the GOAL, it does not make the SCRIPT honest. Any other caller of --check on a non-POSIX box still gets a misleading exit code, and the next person to read that exit code inherits the same wrong conclusion the precondition did.

CAUTION FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS, measured during g-115-9360: obeying the parent goal's own instruction (run --check, then run it without --check) creates a HALF-BUILT .venv inside the product checkout Ayoai-Environment-Processor — step 1 venv create succeeds, step 2 dies on a missing bin/pip. That was NOT run on this box and should not be run on a Windows box now.

Related class: guard-6182 (the never-FAILABLE precondition, inverse polarity of guard-5057).

g-372-28.title: Resolve hypothesis: was the /srv 400 GiB jump the cutover import, or a sustained fill rate?
g-372-28.description: Pre-registered during g-372-22. Read `df -B1 /srv` on zakbox1 (ssh rack — `ssh zakbox1` does not resolve) on or after 2026-09-23. g-115-8851.title: Apply: correct the store-hygiene goal description's universal .history recovery-layer claim — it is absent for 3 of 4 capped stores, and 30,588 records were destroyed in one run with no snapshot
g-115-8851.description:
RELAYED by alpha worker Body (spark_capture from g-115-1651), filed at reducer spark replay 2026-09-04.

THE CLAIM. The recurring goal g-115-1651's description states, without qualification: 'Recovery layer is the .history snapshot taken inside the same locked write (tiered, non-expiring)'.

MEASURED FALSE for 3 of the 4 stores that capped in one run (alpha worker Body, hostname cc-09, uname -r 6.8.0-138-generic, 2026-09-04T05:2x, occurrence 46). Of 37 stores swept and 14 that acted, four used mode=cap with archive:None, so the .history snapshot is their ONLY possible recovery layer. Probing each with history.py list: meta/gate-firings.jsonl (5,975 dropped) NO HISTORY; world/presence/alpha.jsonl (21,376 dropped) NO HISTORY; world/presence/foxtrot.jsonl (3,237 dropped) NO HISTORY; meta/history-save-telemetry.jsonl (43,181 dropped) HISTORY PRESENT, one version, 14,486,363 bytes, stamped 2026-09-04T05-22-48 by this very sweep. So 30,588 records were permanently destroyed in that run with no archive sibling and no snapshot.

TWO POSITIVE CONTROLS make the absence real rather than a blind instrument: the history-save-telemetry snapshot above was written seconds earlier by the same run, and world/knowledge/tree/_tree.yaml returns 191 versions — so history.py resolves subdirectory paths fine. (The worker nearly concluded subdirectory files were untracked; .history/snapshots holds knowledge, team-state, telemetry and audit-reports directory trees, which falsified that.) world/presence has ZERO coverage under .history/snapshots and there is NO exclusion rule for it in _fileops.py or history.py.

WHETHER THE LOSS ITSELF IS WRONG IS A SEPARATE QUESTION and the worker explicitly does not assert it is: store-hygiene.yaml classifies presence as reader-unwired + disposable + recency-semantics, and gate-firings as age-capped at 40d because all four of its readers window 30d. Both are defensible. THE DEFECT IS THE UNIVERSAL SAFETY CLAIM in the operating instructions, because that is the sentence a reader relies on when deciding whether it is safe to enable a NEW store under this sweep — i.e. an archive-before-delete.md step-2 violation waiting to be inherited.

NOTE THE RECURRENCE: this same description ALREADY documents itself making exactly this error once — its prior sentence 'Every store ships DISABLED, so the sweep is a safe no-op' is recorded as 'true at filing, false for at least the last two fires, BOTH of which re-derived the real state from the config because nobody corrected the source'. Same failure mode, different sentence, same file.

THE FIX IS TWO-PART: (1) correct the description to say the recovery layer is PER-STORE and must be read from store-hygiene.yaml; (2) decide, separately, whether any cap-with-no-archive store should acquire one.

NOT OWNED BY g-358-10 (checked; the dedup probe's DECLINE citing it is a FALSE match — g-358-10 deletes expired gate-firings date segments).

g-115-7047.title: Two Bodies of the SAME agent executed one goal to completion simultaneously — in_flight is agent-keyed without a SID and claimed_by_sid lags across boxes, so nothing joins them
g-115-7047.description:
Relayed by alpha worker Body (spark_capture from g-335-1339), filed at reducer spark replay 2026-08-21. Two relays, the second correcting the first.

MEASURED TIMELINE (cc-07): goal g-335-1339 filed by zeta 22:30:48; the goal record's `started` stamp read 22:50:25 with `last_modified` 22:54:15 (another Body already mid-execution); aspirations-claim.sh SUCCEEDED at 22:57:06 with NO conflict; the other Body's production Lambda fix landed on origin/main as abce8c6 at 23:05:15 while this Body was still implementing. Discovered only by a voluntary `git log origin/main` before pushing — nothing in the loop surfaced it.

THE CORRECTION THAT NARROWS IT: the peer was NOT another agent. The goal's outcome_note is signed 'alpha (worker Body, cc-08)' — alpha's OWN sibling Body. zeta was only the filer of pre-execution context. So one agent's two Bodies independently designed, tested and shipped the same production fix on two boxes within ~15 minutes.

MECHANISM, and why neither existing signal can catch it: worker-loop Phase 4c states team-state `in_flight` is AGENT-KEYED WITH NO SID (which is exactly why 4a's clear is a --if-goal compare-and-swap: a worker and its reducer share one row BY DESIGN). That sharing prevents one Body blanking another's row, but the same property means the agent-level row cannot represent two Bodies holding different goals and cannot flag two Bodies holding the SAME goal. The goal-level claimed_by_sid CAN discriminate and did not, because of own-cloud cross-box read lag. So the two signals fail in complementary directions — in_flight is fresh but not sid-discriminating; claimed_by_sid is sid-discriminating but stale across boxes — and nothing joins them.

SECOND INSTANCE, different shape, same unit: on g-350-176 this Body read claimed_by=None, wrote a defer_reason, and the write response revealed a partner Body (SID ed59f154) had claimed it 30s BEFORE the read returned. So both the CLAIM path and the READ path can miss a live peer.

SCOPE IT AS INTRA-AGENT BODY COORDINATION, not cross-agent claim propagation — same agent, same store, and a shared in_flight row already exists, so it is the tractable half.

CHEAP CANDIDATE REMEDY (not a mandate — measure first): at Phase 2.9, immediately after claiming, re-read the goal record ONCE and compare claimed_by_sid to $MIND_SID; if it names a different sid with a newer stamp, release and re-select. That is one extra read on a path that already reads the record. Note the claim response ALREADY carried a `started` stamp 7 minutes older than the claim and nothing asked anyone to look at it — surfacing started/last_modified drift at claim time may be cheaper still.

RELATED BUT NOT THE SAME (checked before filing): g-115-5208 (claimed_by_sid present on only 13%% of the newest cohort) and g-115-6998 (a writer CLEARS claimed_by while claimed_by_sid survives) both concern the field's population/lifecycle; neither covers two Bodies of one agent executing one goal concurrently.

COST HERE WAS NET-POSITIVE BY LUCK, NOT DESIGN: the duplicate implementation became a review that caught a real defect in the shipped one (a presence-only monitor predicate satisfiable by an identity-less row). The same race on two Bodies editing one file is a merge conflict at best and silent divergence at worst.

-- ADDENDUM (alpha reducer, cc-04, 2026-09-05, spark_capture replay; source: alpha worker Body on DESKTOP-O91DLK2) --

SECOND INDEPENDENT OCCURRENCE, on g-370-37, plus a SECOND CANDIDATE MECHANISM this goal's title does not cover and a one-command discriminating probe.

TIMELINE (from the record and the Body's own tool output, both Bodies on DESKTOP-O91DLK2): ~15:20 read g-370-37 via `aspirations-query --goal-field id --full` -> status=pending, claimed_by=None, claimed_by_sid=None. 15:24:35 `aspirations-claim.sh g-370-37 alpha --source world --deviation precondition-fail` SUCCEEDED, returning executed_by_sid=1ea279dd and claimed_at 2026-09-05T15:24:35. ~12 minutes of verification followed (source read of promotion-day.sh, a dry run on Ayoai-Environment-Server, the host-capability probe, an end-to-end dry run on Vinheim-Web-App). At ~15:36 the record read status=completed, completed_date 2026-09-05, completed_by_sid=fc37233d-d2f5-46dc-95f9-543423b0aa24, completed_by_role=worker, claimed_by=None — a DIFFERENT Body of the same agent had closed it, and its appended note is stamped 15:19Z, BEFORE the claim. Duplication was TOTAL, not partial: the same five-repo dry run and the same adjacent sq-013 finding, derived independently.

TWO CANDIDATE DEFECTS, stated separately because the Body did not isolate which fired:
(1) THE CLAIM ENDPOINT MAY ACCEPT A CLAIM ON AN ALREADY-COMPLETED GOAL. The 15:24:35 claim succeeded and the peer's close is stamped 15:19Z, so unless the close landed inside the read->claim window, a TERMINAL goal was claimable. This is not the agent-keyed in_flight mechanism in this goal's title — it is the claim being ACCEPTED at all.
(2) The peer executed from ~13:57 through 15:19 with claimed_by=None visible to the other Body's read, so either it worked unclaimed or its claim was not visible in the store that was read.

Either way the invariant a worker relies on — "SELECT offers only unclaimed goals, and a successful claim means the unit is mine" — did not hold.

DISCRIMINATING PROBE for whoever takes this, one call: invoke the claim endpoint against a goal whose status is already completed and read the response. If it returns success rather than an error, defect (1) is real and the fix is a one-line guard at the claim endpoint (refuse terminal status) — which also bounds (2)'s blast radius.

RELATED BUT NOT THE SAME: guard-1460 says another SESSION of this agent can hold a claim and claimed_by_sid is the discriminator — that governs READING a claim, not accepting one.

COST: ~12 minutes and a 3,931-char duplicate append to an already-closed goal (independent corroboration, so noise rather than harm). In general unbounded on a long unit, and INVISIBLE to both Bodies at the time — this was found only because the Body re-read the record before closing. NOT MEASURED: whether the stranded-claim sweep or an LWW shard merge cleared the claim rather than the peer's close doing it.
[appended:ADDENDUM-20260905-alpha-cc04-g370-37-occurrence]

CROSS-REFERENCE (alpha reducer, g-306-284 occ210 spark replay, 2026-09-25): a worker relay from g-306-322 (2026-08-19) reports a sibling path into this same collision class. unit-claim.sh (worker-loop Phase 2.95) is wired into the WORKER path only; the reducer executes goals through aspirations-execute Phase 4 with no unit-claim. Re-checked at filing: 'unit-claim' appears in none of aspirations-execute/SKILL.md, execute-protocol-digest.md, aspirations-loop-digest.md or aspirations/SKILL.md. So a reducer executing a goal wholesale cannot see a worker Body holding a unit lease on it. Related: g-115-10649 (one unit token granted to two SIDs 1s apart), g-115-9130 (a worker verify_verdict is lost when no unit-claim anchor exists).
[appended:xref-g-306-322-reducer-unit-claim]

pairs.label: F1
pairs.relay: mutation-proof-test.sh LEAVES ITS BACKUPS IN THE TARGET REPO'S WORKING TREE, and product-pr-flow.sh stages with `git add -A`. Those two facts compose into a near-miss I hit on g-364-04 (2026-08-21). After 6 partition mutations plus one direct run against /opt/GitHub/Zak-Data-Solutions/Vinheim-Web-App, five untracked files remained: amplify/backend.ts.mutation-backup.{18111,18506} and amplify/functions/user-migration/handler.ts.mutation-backup.{16908,17303,17698}. Each was byte-identical to its restored target, so the RESTORE guarantee held perfectly -- the tool's headline promise is intact and this is not a data-loss defect. The exposure is downstream: the very next canonical step for product work is product-pr-flow.sh, whose step 3 is `git add -A`, so five stray copies of production source would have been committed into the PR and merged. I removed them by hand only because I ran `git status` for an unrelated reason (checking origin/main freshness). Nothing in either script's contract would have surfaced them, and a reviewer skimming a diff that already touches those exact files is unlikely to notice two extra copies of them.

pairs.label: F2
pairs.relay: WHEN EXPLAINING WHY A PIPELINE DID NOT ACT, READ ITS AUDIT TRAIL BEFORE ITS SOURCE. A prior session answered 'why was this alert never triaged?' by reading alert-sweep.sh, finding a genuine newest-N scan window with no watermark, and concluding eviction. The mechanism is real, self-consistent, well-documented in the script's own comments, and WRONG for this case — and it was emailed to the user as the explanation. One query against the ledger falsified it in seconds: the mail was read on four separate sweeps that day and each row says log_other, i.e. seen-and-classified-as-nothing. The code tells you what CAN happen; the audit trail tells you what DID. A code-derived mechanism is especially seductive here because it explains the symptom perfectly and cites real code — there is no felt uncertainty to prompt a second look. Generalization: for any 'why did X not happen' question about a system that keeps a ledger, the ledger is signal 1 and the source is signal 2, not the reverse.

pairs.label: F3
pairs.relay: A verification precondition that tests only file mtime (`find ... -mmin -5`) CANNOT distinguish an in-progress run from a just-finished one: the run's FINAL write refreshes mtime, so for the whole window after ANY run ends the gate reports a live window that does not exist. Measured on g-326-526 (cc-07, 2026-09-07): pc-live-processor-run returned rc=0 while the matched run_status.json read status failed, endTime 18:44:13 — ended ~4 minutes before the probe. This is why successive passes of that goal each found the window open and then found nothing running. WORK FOR AN OWNER: (a) amend pc-live-processor-run to require the status field too — pattern already positive- AND negative-controlled against the real serialization: -exec grep -l '"status"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"running"' {} + (negative control on the real failed file 0 matches rc=1; positive control on a status-flipped copy 1 match rc=0); it is NOT installed because no run_status.json anywhere currently carries status running, so the end-to-end control is unrun (guard-2421). (b) SWEEP for the class: any other precondition or gate whose liveness test is mtime-only has the same false positive.

pairs.label: F4
pairs.relay: A predicate whose `type` is `command_succeeds` reports `observed_value` as an EXIT CODE, so `observed_value: 0` + `passed: true` means SATISFIED -- but on g-326-526 the pc-live-processor-run predicate is being used to answer a COUNTING question (are there live Processor runs?), and a prior Body read the same 0 as a count and concluded the opposite. Two Bodies, two opposite verdicts, one unchanged output; the goal has been frozen across both. THE GENERAL DEFECT: a count-shaped question wired into a command_succeeds predicate produces a gate that ALWAYS passes (any successfully-executed probe exits 0 whether or not it found anything), so the precondition cannot gate and precondition-defer-recheck will read the goal as unblocked forever. WHERE TO LOOK: any verification.preconditions entry of type command_succeeds whose predicate_id names a quantity (pc-live-*, pc-*-count, pc-has-*). The settling test is one turn: run the predicate command by hand beside predicate.py and print stdout, BYTE COUNT and rc together (guard-2298) -- the shape tells a count from an rc immediately. Suggested title: Investigate: command_succeeds preconditions used for counting questions cannot gate -- audit predicate_ids naming a quantity.

pairs.label: F5
pairs.relay: A TWO-POINT TREND WRITTEN INTO A DEFER NARRATIVE BECAME STANDING STRATEGY GUIDANCE, AND THE THIRD POINT REVERSED IT. g-326-526 defer 2026-08-31 observed a shrinking artifact population (runs_dirs 8->4, run_status 10->4 across two probes) and generalised it to a RULE for future re-probers: run artifacts are being garbage-collected, so waiting does NOT accumulate evidence. Measured 2026-09-05 on the third point: runs_dirs 4->23, run_status 4->33, accounts 71->80 - the population grew 8x in five days. The dip was noise, not a GC regime. The lesson is not about this goal: a defer narrative is READ AS AUTHORITATIVE by every later re-prober (that is its purpose), so an inference drawn there from n=2 propagates as policy and actively discourages the re-probing that would falsify it. When recording a trend in a defer, state the point COUNT and label an n=2 slope as provisional; a defer is the wrong place to generalise from.

pairs.label: F9
pairs.relay:
FILING-SHAPED RELAY (Case B, sq-013). THE FLEET RE-DERIVES defer_reason GATES ON A CADENCE AND RE-DERIVES PR-BODY GATES NEVER — so a hand-written 'MERGE GATE — do not merge' section in a PR body is a permanent stop with no expiry and no owner.

MEASURED 2026-08-21, cc-07 (alpha worker Body, g-363-64). Concrete instance: zkysar1/Ayoai-Environment-Server PR #246 carried a hand-written merge gate whose underlying hazard (guard-4299, EFS cross-client rename -> ESTALE on a running JVM) had been closed by g-326-366's instance-local JAR pin the DAY BEFORE the gate was written. Two goals (g-115-7050, g-115-7051) were closed without merging because both agents re-checked the gate's stated CONDITION and neither re-derived whether the condition was still a REASON. ~2 days stranded on a verified revenue-instrumentation fix. Full lesson in the paired spark entry.

WHY THIS IS A REAL GAP AND NOT JUST ONE AGENT'S MISS. The fleet has genuine machinery for exactly this problem on the goal surface: reclaim-routed-work.md names the PREMISE vs RULE axes explicitly, gates/defer_scope.py and defer-scope-coverage.py exist, aspirations-precheck Phase 0.5b re-probes deferred goals every iteration, and capability-gate.py refuses agent-provisionable defers at write time. ALL of it keys on the goal record. A gate that lives in a PR BODY is invisible to every one of those layers — there is no field to scan, no cadence that opens it, and completed-not-committed-sweep reads PR bodies only with a KEYWORD scan whose whole known weakness (guard-3816) is that a correctly-stated gate is often keyword-invisible.

Note the asymmetry that makes it self-concealing: the sweep's keyword scan produces FALSE MERGE INSTRUCTIONS when it misses a gate (the g-115-7051 case, already known and guarded). The failure I am reporting is the OPPOSITE direction and has no guard: when the gate IS seen and honoured, nothing ever re-opens it. Honouring a gate looks like correct behaviour every single time, so the stall accrues silently and no audit counts it.

SUGGESTED WORK, cheapest first:
(a) When a merge gate must be written into a PR body, require it to name the CONSEQUENCE, not just the CONDITION — 'do not merge because X breaks Y' invites the next reader to check whether X still breaks Y; 'do not merge until no session is live' terminates in a clean re-check and never surfaces the rule axis. This is a one-line convention change to whatever writes these sections, and it is the highest-leverage half.
(b) A sweep over OPEN draft PRs across the product estate that are older than N days and carry a hand-written gate section: report each with the age of its gate and the goal ids that cite it. Report-only; the point is to make the population visible, since right now nobody can even count it.
(c) Consider whether a PR-body gate should be REQUIRED to cite a goal id that owns clearing it. PR #246's gate named who could clear it ('the Environment Server is alpha's lane, live sessions are foxtrot's') but no goal, so there was no queue entry anywhere that would ever come up for selection.

SUGGESTED TITLE: 'A merge gate written into a PR body has no expiry and no re-derivation cadence — the defer-reason reclaim machinery does not reach the PR surface (measured: PR #246 stranded ~2 days past its hazard being fixed)'.

DEDUP EVIDENCE: I did NOT run a title scan for this before relaying, because the relay is the sanctioned Case-B channel and the reducer's sq-013 handler dedups before filing. Whoever files it should scan for 'merge gate', 'PR body', 'draft PR' and 'guard-3816' first — g-115-6259 ('Recover the g-326-170 test commit stranded on unmergeable PR #201') is adjacent and is NOT this: it is one stranded commit, not the missing cadence.

pairs.label: G1
pairs.relay: STORE-HYGIENE SWEEP DESTROYS RECORDS WITH NO RECOVERY LAYER WHILE ITS OWN INSTRUCTIONS PROMISE ONE. The recurring goal g-115-1651 description states, without qualification: "Recovery layer is the .history snapshot taken inside the same locked write (tiered, non-expiring)". MEASURED FALSE for 3 of the 4 stores that capped this run (alpha worker Body, hostname cc-09, uname -r 6.8.0-138-generic, 2026-09-04T05:2x, occurrence 46). Of 37 stores swept and 14 that acted, four used mode=cap with archive:None, so the .history snapshot is their ONLY possible recovery layer. Probing each with history.py list: meta/gate-firings.jsonl (5,975 dropped) NO HISTORY; world/presence/alpha.jsonl (21,376 dropped) NO HISTORY; world/presence/foxtrot.jsonl (3,237 dropped) NO HISTORY; meta/history-save-telemetry.jsonl (43,181 dropped) HISTORY PRESENT, one version, 14,486,363 bytes, stamped 2026-09-04T05-22-48 by this very sweep. So 30,588 records were permanently destroyed this run with no archive sibling and no snapshot. TWO POSITIVE CONTROLS make the absence real rather than a blind instrument: the history-save-telemetry snapshot above was written seconds earlier by the same run, and world/knowledge/tree/_tree.yaml returns 191 versions, so history.py resolves subdirectory paths fine (I nearly concluded subdirectory files were untracked; .history/snapshots holds knowledge, team-state, telemetry and audit-reports directory trees, which falsified that). world/presence has zero coverage under .history/snapshots and there is NO exclusion rule for it in _fileops.py or history.py. WHETHER THE LOSS ITSELF IS WRONG IS A SEPARATE QUESTION and I am not asserting it is: store-hygiene.yaml classifies presence as reader-unwired + disposable + recency-semantics, and gate-firings as age-capped at 40d because all four of its readers window 30d. Both are defensible. THE DEFECT IS THE UNIVERSAL SAFETY CLAIM in the operating instructions, because that is the sentence a reader relies on when deciding whether it is safe to enable a NEW store under this sweep. NOTE THE RECURRENCE: this description ALREADY documents itself making exactly this error once — its prior sentence "Every store ships DISABLED, so the sweep is a safe no-op" is recorded as "true at filing, false for at least the last two fires, BOTH of which re-derived the real state from the config because nobody corrected the source". Same failure mode, different sentence, same file. SUGGESTED TITLE: "Fix: store-hygiene goal description claims a universal .history recovery layer that is absent for 3 of 4 capped stores". The fix is two-part: correct the description to say the recovery layer is per-store and must be read from store-hygiene.yaml, and decide (separately) whether any cap-with-no-archive store should acquire one.

pairs.label: G2
pairs.relay: TWO BODIES EXECUTED g-335-1339 CONCURRENTLY AND BOTH SHIPPED, AND THE CLAIM DID NOT PREVENT IT. Timeline measured on cc-07: goal filed by zeta 22:30:48; goal record's `started` stamp 22:50:25 with `last_modified` 22:54:15 (another Body already executing); my aspirations-claim.sh SUCCEEDED at 22:57:06 with no conflict; the other Body's fix landed on origin/main as abce8c6 at 23:05:15 while I was mid-implementation. I discovered it only because I checked `git log origin/main` before pushing -- nothing in the loop surfaced it. SECOND INSTANCE THE SAME UNIT, different shape: on g-350-176 I read claimed_by=None, wrote a defer_reason, and the write response showed a partner Body (SID ed59f154) had claimed it 30s BEFORE my read returned. So both the CLAIM path and the READ path can miss a live peer. Consistent with own-cloud store propagation lag between boxes -- a claim written on box A is not necessarily visible to box B's next read, and aspirations-claim.sh has no cross-box compare-and-swap that would refuse. COST HERE WAS BOUNDED AND ACTUALLY POSITIVE (my independent implementation became a review that caught a real defect in theirs -- see the predicate-vs-purpose relay), but that is luck, not design: the same race on two agents editing the same file would be a merge conflict at best and silent divergence at worst. WHAT TO FILE: a pre-execution freshness re-read of the claim immediately before Phase 3 work begins (cheap: one read), and/or surfacing `started`/`last_modified` drift at claim time -- the claim response ALREADY carried a `started` stamp 7 minutes older than my own claim and nothing in the loop asked me to look at it. Suggested title: 'Fix: aspirations-claim.sh succeeds against a goal another Body is already executing -- claim visibility lags across boxes on own-cloud'.

pairs.label: G2b
pairs.relay: CORRECTION + MECHANISM for the concurrent-execution relay on g-335-1339 (the entry immediately prior, 'TWO BODIES EXECUTED g-335-1339 CONCURRENTLY'): I wrote it as though the peer were another AGENT. It was not. Reading the goal's outcome_note at close time, the first half is signed 'EXECUTION CLOSE 2026-08-20T23:1x by alpha (worker Body, cc-08)' -- ALPHA'S OWN SIBLING BODY. zeta was only the FILER of the pre-execution context. So one agent's two Bodies independently designed, tested and shipped a production Lambda fix for the same goal, on two boxes, within ~15 minutes. THIS NARROWS THE DEFECT AND NAMES A MECHANISM. worker-loop Phase 4c states that team-state in_flight is AGENT-KEYED WITH NO SID, which is exactly why 4a's clear is a --if-goal compare-and-swap: a worker and its reducer SHARE one in_flight row by construction. That sharing is designed to prevent one Body blanking another's row -- but the same property means the agent-level row cannot represent two Bodies of one agent holding DIFFERENT goals, and cannot flag two Bodies holding the SAME goal. The goal-level claimed_by_sid can distinguish them and did not, because of the own-cloud read lag already measured in the prior entry. So the two signals fail in complementary directions: in_flight is fresh but not sid-discriminating; claimed_by_sid is sid-discriminating but stale across boxes. Neither alone can answer 'is a sibling Body already on this goal', and nothing joins them. WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE FILING: scope it as INTRA-AGENT Body coordination (tractable -- same agent, same store, shared in_flight row already exists) rather than cross-agent claim propagation (harder). A cheap concrete candidate: at Phase 2.9, after claiming, re-read the goal record ONCE and compare claimed_by_sid to $MIND_SID -- if it names a different sid with a newer stamp, release and re-select. That is a single extra read on the path that already reads the record. COST MEASURED HERE: a complete duplicate implementation of a production fix (design, tests, review) on cc-07 while cc-08 shipped abce8c6. It ended net-positive only because my duplicate became a review that found a real defect in theirs (the presence-only-predicate relay) -- luck, not design, and it will not repeat reliably.
